page.layout: One printed page, one column of text. Top: running head "AUB. MIRÆO." with page number 161 at the right. Below that, a fragment of the address to the recipient (full width). Then the heading "EPIST. XII.", a summary in hanging-indent type, the salutation in italics, and the body in one column. Catchword "ut" at the lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: stræ studiosissimus Aubertus Miræus
Decanus Antverp. indignus.
EPIST. XII.
Joh. Morinus, Aub. Miraeo similiter gra-
tias agit de libris, quibus ipsum donaverat Miraeus.
Joh. Morinus, Aub. Miræo S. D.
Cum primum Lugduno Lutetiam ve-
ni, redditæ mihi sunt literæ tuæ,
quibus Exercitiones meas Ecclesiasticas,
te accepisse cognovi, sed literæ, quas ad
te miseram, serius in manus tuas per-
venerunt, tibi tamen postea datas esse
nihil ambigo. Plurimum mihi gratulor,
quod tibi viro in omni scientiarum genere
versatissimo placent exercitationes
meæ; ea enim es eruditione, & apud omnes
eruditos æstimatione, ut nulli aut
pauci improbaturi sint, quæ tuo calculo
comprobas. Itaq; ut alia atque etiam ma-
jora tentare audeam in hoc scriptionis
genere, tua cohortatione facis, addisque

page.notes: The first word of the summary line "donaverat" is partly covered by an ink blot on the left; the first letter is unreadable. The printed "es eruditione" is likely a misprint for "est" but is copied as printed. "Exercitiones" and "Itaq;" are printed as such. The summary is treated as a level 2 title above the letter. Show-through and the neighbouring page's edge on the right are left out.
